### GET `/v1/projects/{projectId}/api-keys`

**List the API keys in a project**

Newest first. Revoked and expired keys are included and labelled by `status`; the secret is never returned here, only `key_prefix`. Paged with the canonical envelope `{ data, has_more, next_offset }` - BREAKING: `count` was removed. Read `has_more` before concluding you have seen every credential in the project, and pass `next_offset` back as `offset` to continue; it is null on the last page.

**Auth:** signed-in dashboard session (cookie).

#### Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `projectId` | path | string | yes |  | Project id, `proj_…`. |
| `limit` | query | number | no | 1 to 200 | Page size. Clamped to 200 by the repository regardless. |
| `offset` | query | number | no | min 0 |  |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | [ApiKeyDto](./schemas.md#apikeydto)[] | yes |  |  |
| `data[].id` | string | yes |  |  |
| `data[].project_id` | string | yes |  |  |
| `data[].name` | string | yes |  |  |
| `data[].key_prefix` | string | yes |  | The first 12 characters of the key. Safe to display and to log; never enough to reconstruct the credential. |
| `data[].environment` | string | yes | one of `test`, `live` | Always equal to the project's environment; the ingest path re-checks the pair. |
| `data[].status` | string | yes | one of `active`, `expired`, `revoked` | Derived from `revoked_at`/`expires_at` at read time, exactly as the ingest path derives it. `active` here still does not mean the key works: a suspended or deleted project refuses every key under it. |

Read `effective_scopes` to find out what the key may do now. The ingest path does NOT consult scopes today - it authenticates on the key, its project and its environment - so an empty list is a normal ingest key. |
| `data[].effective_scopes` | string[] | yes |  | WHAT THIS KEY MAY ACTUALLY DO: `scopes` intersected with the permissions its issuer holds RIGHT NOW. A key minted by a developer who has since been demoted to viewer, or removed from the organization, reports fewer scopes here than it was minted with - and an EMPTY list once the issuer is gone entirely. ### POST `/v1/projects/{projectId}/api-keys`

**Issue an API key**

THE ONLY RESPONSE THAT EVER CONTAINS THE PLAINTEXT KEY. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored, so it cannot be shown again by this or any other endpoint - show it to the user once and let them copy it. The environment is taken from the project (wk_test_ for a test project, wk_live_ for a live one) and cannot be chosen. Rate limited, and subject to a per-project ceiling (`MAX_API_KEYS_PER_PROJECT`) that counts un-revoked keys.

**Auth:** signed-in dashboard session (cookie).

#### Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `projectId` | path | string | yes |  | Project id, `proj_…`. |

#### Request body

`application/json`, required - [CreateApiKeyDto](./schemas.md#createapikeydto)

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | max 200 chars | How an operator will recognise this key in the list. Shown in audit entries. |
| `expires_at` | string | no | format `date-time` | Must be in the future. The key stops authenticating at this instant with no further action; omit for a key that only revocation ends. |
| `scopes` | string[] | no |  | Control-plane permissions this key may hold. Each must be a real permission AND one the caller holds themselves - a key cannot be minted with more authority than the person minting it. Defaults to none, which is what an ingest-only key wants. |

### POST `/v1/projects/{projectId}/api-keys/{apiKeyId}/revoke`

**Revoke an API key**

Takes effect immediately: the ingest path refuses the key on its next request. The row is kept with `revoked_at` set, so the delivery history it produced stays attributable. Idempotent - revoking an already-revoked key returns it unchanged.
